jurisdiction.publisher: Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB / BST), Gatineau, Quebec

domain: railway safety - prediction of casualty outcomes of reported rail occurrences (Canada, federal)
prediction_question: A railway occurrence begins at a known place, time and operating context on the Canadian network (crossing accident, derailment, trespasser event, fire, collision, movement exceeding limits of authority, ...). At that instant, given only pre-occurrence context - where (subdivision, nearest location, province, region, lat/long), which railway, when (date, time of day, season), and what the train was doing (activity type) - will the occurrence result in at least one casualty (fatality or any injury)?
prediction_time: The instant the occurrence begins (OccDate/OccTime, with the documented local time zone via TimeZoneID). Everything the TSB records during or after the occurrence is excluded from the shipped features: TSB's accident/incident type assignment (its taxonomy embeds outcomes, e.g. 'NON-MAIN-TRACK TRAIN DERAILMENT (NO DAMAGE)'), all injury/DG-release/fire/evacuation/damage flags and counts, weather observations taken at the occurrence, track and rolling-stock attributes measured during the occurrence, investigation/deployment/closeout fields, process dates (ENTRY_DT, RELEASE_DT, DAILY_RELEASED_DT, OccClosedDate), the free-text Summary, and even ReportedDate/ReportedTime (the notification instant, which post-dates the onset) - the last is shipped only in the record's provenance, never as a feature. The casualty outcome unfolds after onset and is the label.
target_definition: Binary: occurrence resulted in >=1 casualty. Label source columns: InjuriesIND ('Injuries indicator'), cross-checked against TotalFatalInjuries / TotalSeriousInjuries / TotalMinorInjuries ('Total fatal/serious/minor injuries') and the separate INJURIES table (RODSdb_MDOTW_VW_INJURIES_PUBLIC.csv, 2,710,400 bytes). All are excluded from the shipped feature columns by construction.

split_strategy: Proposed (windows to be recomputed on the full panel on the worker at construction - counts below are measured on bounded 2 MB samples, not the full file). Panel: occurrences 1983-01..2026-08 (file vintage: released 2026-09-15, data through the preceding month-end). Construction would start the panel at a modern-era boundary (2004-01 proposed; the 1983-1990s rows are shaped differently - in the 1.5 MB tail sample of 1983-84 rows: injuries 30.2%, accident types include 'DG LEAKER' (343/1450) and 'HISTORICAL' (120), time zone 'N/A', OccClassID 'N/A' - so early years need separate treatment or exclusion). Proposed windows, occurrences by onset date: train 2004-01..2021-12, eval 2022-01..2024-12, holdout 2025-01..2026-08. Both classes present in every era window by measured sample injury rates: 13.9% (2008-10 sample, n=1,499), 15.0% (2001-02, n=1,359), 18.0% (1995, n=1,383), 14.7% (2025-26, n=1,501). Occurrences are independent single events (no storm-style clustering); each row is one occurrence; multiple casualties within one occurrence do not duplicate rows. Row key: OccID (occurrence identification number; OccNo like 'R26E0080' as secondary). At ~1,100-1,500 occurrences/year in the modern era, each window carries thousands of rows; exact per-window counts are a construction-time measurement.

Other outcome flags in the 2025-26 sample: FireIND 7.4%, DerailedRSIND 48.4%, DGCarsInvolvedIND 8.4%, EvacuationIND 0.2%, DGReleasedCarsIND 0.1% - which rules out DG-release (3/year per the publisher's own 2025 summary) and evacuation as primary labels; casualty is the right label.
measurements.publisher_cross_check: TSB 2025 annual summary (fetched 2026-10-21): 831 rail accidents in 2025 (895 in 2024; 10-year average 1,007), 332 incidents (303 in 2024), 82 accidents involving dangerous goods, 3 with DG released, 'Freight trains accounted for 42% of all rolling stock involved in rail accidents in 2025'. Sample consistency: the newest 2 MB sample holds 665 rows from 2025 and 836 from 2026 (to 2026-09-05) - consistent in order of magnitude with 831+332=1,163 occurrences in 2025. Full-panel accident/incident counts must be cross-checked against these published figures at construction.

measurements.novelty_prior_art: Web search 2026-10-21: (1) NRC/CNR publication 'Development of a daily updated train derailment impact map...' - a risk-mapping tool built on RODS historical counts, explicitly deferring predictive derailment models to future work; (2) Rana, Sattari, Lefsrud & Hendry (2024), 'Machine Learning Approach to Enhance Highway Railroad Grade Crossing Safety by Analyzing Crash Data and Identifying Hotspot Crash Locations' (doi:10.1177/03611981231212162) - ML analysis of grade-crossing casualty severity from TSB/RODS data, a research paper, not a shipped dataset/benchmark; (3) TSB's own statistics products are descriptive. No public ML-ready rail-occurrence prediction dataset with splits and a scored contract found; mechanical catalog search recorded via check-novelty.py.
measurements.cost_measured: Coordinator discovery cost: 8 ranged HTTP requests (5 size probes + dictionary + 4 era samples + tail) ~= 8.6 MB transferred, <60 s wall clock. Construction cost on the worker: one ~157 MB fetch of 5 CSVs plus joins; trivial for a Hetzner worker; the bytes never pass through the coordinator.

Fixed for tsb-002: era signal = taxonomy alone; tz-missingness recorded per year as a separate property; per-year diagnostics now written before the assertion so a failed run still uploads evidence.

exit 2 in 28 s on the same guard, now with the evidence uploaded: the taxonomy-only era signal still measures the panel start at 2016 (era share 2.3% at 2015, 0.58% at 2016, 0% from 2017), outside the asserted [1995, 2010] band. Not a mechanical defect: the 2% rule and the asserted band are inconsistent on the full panel, and the resolution (re-pin the band to 2016 or re-derive the rule from shipped-feature completeness) is a recorded design decision in next_action, owned by the construction session.

exit 2 in 28 s: the re-pinned band worked - panel start measured 2016-01-01, inside [2014, 2018] - and the build reached the split stage for the first time on full data (train 7,925 / eval 3,831 / holdout 1,976; pre-window 56,865, post-window 109; 7 non-identical OccNo collisions handled, 0 empty OccNo). Resolution belongs to the construction session: treat the corrupt coordinates as missing with a recorded count, or repair them from the source row evidence.
